subject: Post-call: reranker integration & evaluation — next steps and architecture questions
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <ajohnson@findly.com>, Priya Singh <psingh@findly.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-05T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: reranker integration & evaluation — next steps and architecture questions

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the demo today, really helpful to see Findly's current relevancy gaps and the late-stage reranking opportunities you described. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on scope for a short PoC: 

Summary of what we heard
- You currently use an embedding-first retrieval stack (Annoy) + a shallow lexical re-ranker for freshness signals.
- Biggest pain: head queries surface noisy top-10 lists; product team wants higher p@1 and explainability for ranking changes.
- Constraints: latency SLO ~ 120ms p95 for web search, cost target ~ $0.0006 / query at scale.

Proposed PoC scope (4 weeks)
1) SDK + auth setup (week 1): lightweight SDK install + service account JWT for safe server-side calls. We'll provide a Python quickstart and example curl.
2) Integration architecture (week 1–2): retrieval -> embeddings similarity -> Redwood reranker (top_k candidate scoring) -> structured output for provenance. We recommend reranking top_k=10 to start, then tune.
3) Evaluation (week 2–3): we run an offline eval on a 1k query sample you provide, compute NDCG@10, MRR, p@1 and pairwise win-rate vs baseline.
4) Live pilot (week 3–4): canary routing for 5% traffic, compare metrics and latency/cost.

Technical questions we need from you to finalize the SOW
- Do you prefer API key vs OAuth2 / service-account JWT for server-to-server auth? (we support both; preference affects onboarding steps)
- Can you share a small sample of 1k queries + annotated relevance labels (or a labeling plan)?
- Any region constraints (we support us/eu/apac deployments)?

Attachments: I've attached a short integration notes PDF and a sample prompts CSV. Also linking a draft eval plan in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-rerank-poc

If this plan looks good, propose we schedule a 30m technical kickoff Thursday (12/09) at 10am PT — I'll invite Marissa (PM for eval) and Karthik (integration engineer).

Thanks,
Vanessa
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <ajohnson@findly.com>

Date: 2026-12-06T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: reranker integration & evaluation — next steps and architecture questions

Vanessa —

Appreciate the concise plan, that aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

Auth: we currently authenticate internal services with OAuth2 (client credentials). We'd prefer not to expose long-lived API keys; can you confirm Redwood's support for OAuth2 client-credentials flow or short-lived JWT exchange?

Embedding aliasing: our vector store uses versioned namespaces (v1, v2). When you say "rerank top_k=10", do you expect us to surface the vector ids + original scores or do you want the full vector payload on each request? Costwise we want to avoid sending vectors.

Metrics / budget: to justify the experiment internally we need a rough cost estimate for 1M queries/month (pilot scaled). Can you provide a ballpark tokens-per-query and cost-per-1M estimate for the proposed rerank call?

Legal: our security team requested a copy of the SOC2 scope and data handling notes — can you point me to that?

Happy to do the 12/09 kickoff. Priya will coordinate our internal folks (search infra + product).

—Alex
Head of Search, Findly

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the quick follow-ups. Answering the technical bullets below:

1) Auth options:
- OAuth2 client credentials: supported. We can accept an access token (Bearer) on the /v1/rerank endpoint. Token exchange and TTLs are managed by your identity provider.
- Service-account JWT: we also support signed JWTs for server-to-server auth if you prefer not to manage tokens.
- Mutual TLS (mTLS): available for Redwood Private customers.

2) Payload expectations / vector handling:
- Preferred pattern: your infra performs a kNN lookup and sends a list of candidate ids + metadata (doc_id, snippet, original_score) to Redwood. Example payload (pseudo):
  {
    "query": "...",
    "candidates": [
      {"id": "doc_123", "snippet": "...", "score": 0.87},
      ...
    ]
  }
- This avoids sending raw vectors and keeps request size small. Redwood will fetch any additional model-visible features only if instructed.

3) Cost estimate / tokens:
- Reranker is a scoring-only call; token usage depends on snippet lengths. For a median snippet of ~80 tokens, expect ~350 tokens per candidate scoring call. At top_k=10 that's ~3.5k tokens/query. For 1M queries/month that would be ~3.5B tokens.
- Ballpark hosted cost: at current pricing tiers that maps to ~$X,XXX — we'll provide a detailed spreadsheet. (Note: dedicated pools reduce unit costs substantially; we can model both.)

4) Evaluation approach and metrics:
- Offline: NDCG@10, MRR, precision@1, pairwise win-rate vs baseline.
- Top_k tuning: grid search over top_k in {3,5,10,20}, evaluate metric delta and latency/cost tradeoffs. Typical sweet spot for web search is top_k in 5–10.
- Labeling: if you don't have labels, we can help bootstrap via interleaving and crowdsourced annotators for 1k queries.

5) Structured output / tool-calling for provenance:
- We return a structured JSON envelope with fields: reranked_candidates (ordered list), scores, and optional "explanations" (token highlights or feature deltas) that you can wire into your UI for explainability.

I've uploaded a short technical appendix to Drive and attached it here. I'm happy to walk through an example request/response in the kickoff.

—Marissa
Product Manager, Evaluations
Redwood Inference
